finding: §5.3 says the altitude principle is stated in 'SKILL.md and REFERENCE.md, and the --eject-roles default role docs', but tp's --eject-roles writes role JSON files ({id,title,instructions,focus[],domains[]}) with no separate 'docs' artifact. It is unspecified whether 'default role docs' means editing the embedded default reviewer roles' `instructions` text — which would change the per-phase roles_hash for every project on the embedded default corpus and break byte-identity with files ejected before this release — or only updating prose guidance in SKILL.md/REFERENCE.md. §9 (Documentation) lists no role-instructions/corpus change or migration, so an implementer cannot tell whether the default role definitions themselves must be modified.
suggestion: State explicitly that the altitude principle is added only to prose role-authoring guidance (SKILL.md/REFERENCE.md) and NOT to the embedded default role `instructions` (leaving roles_hash and ejected-file byte-identity unaffected); or, if the default role `instructions` do change, say so in §5.3/§9 and specify the roles_hash-staleness / re-eject migration consequence.

finding: §6.3 pins harness_stale for --status (compare the two most recently recorded rounds) and states --record surfaces it 'symmetrically', but never pins whether --record's OWN response includes the round it is recording in the two-round comparison. Test 18 shows --record emits the flag; Test 11 exercises only --status. So `tp review --record <file> --harness-note "B"` after a prior round noted "A" is untestable: one engineer asserts harness_stale=true in that same --record response (just-recorded round counts), another asserts it reflects only rounds recorded before the call (false).
suggestion: State explicitly that --record computes harness_stale AFTER storing the current round's note, so the just-recorded round is the latest of the two compared; add a Test 11/18 case asserting --record's own response reports harness_stale=true when its note differs from the immediately prior recorded round's note.

finding: §6.3 says notes are 'stored verbatim but compared trimmed', and that when harness_stale is true the response carries 'the latest round's harness_note', with 'the recorded note stays in .tp-review/ for audit' (verbatim). It never states whether the EMITTED harness_note is the verbatim stored value or the trimmed value. A test asserting the exact emitted string for a note like '  B  ' is non-deterministic — one engineer asserts '  B  ', another asserts 'B'.
suggestion: Pin the emitted form explicitly: e.g. 'the emitted harness_note is the verbatim stored note (untrimmed); trimming applies only to the non-empty and difference comparisons.' Add a Test 11 assertion on the exact emitted string for a note with surrounding whitespace.

finding: §8.2 branch 3 defines the existing mechanize_candidates threshold as 'a class appearing in at least two rounds, or at least five times in one', but Test 14 (§11) parenthetically redefines it as 'a class recurring in at least two recorded rounds', dropping the five-times-in-one-round alternative. A QA engineer writing the acceptance test from Test 14 would assert a class appearing 5 times in a single round does NOT reach branch 3, contradicting §8.2; two engineers write opposite tests.
suggestion: Make Test 14's parenthetical match §8.2 verbatim: '(a class recurring in at least two recorded rounds, or at least five times in one round)'. Add an explicit acceptance case for the five-times-in-one-round trigger so both threshold branches are pinned.

finding: §9.4 pins the tool's review-loop convergence/instruction strings to fixed wording — 'no surviving critical or high severity finding' (matching review_converge_on: blocking) — and asserts 'no string claims a stop rule the code does not enforce'. But §3.3 makes the policy a resolvable workflow field whose 'all' value is explicitly selectable and enforces 'no finding of any severity survives'. Under review_converge_on=all the code enforces the strict all-severity stop while the fixed string still describes a critical-or-high stop, so the tool's own string then documents a stop rule the code does not enforce — precisely the Principle-1 / §3.1 self-contradiction this release exists to eliminate, reintroduced for the non-default setting. Test 16 only pins the strings to the enforced default (blocking) and never exercises them under all, so the mismatch is untested.
suggestion: Either render the convergence/instruction strings from the resolved review_converge_on ('any surviving finding blocks' under all vs 'critical or high blocks' under blocking), or state in §9.4 that the strings describe the default policy explicitly and note that under all the enforced predicate widens; add a §11 test that the string matches the active setting under all so no string claims an unenforced stop rule for either value.
